title: The AI Ledger
introduction: Reviewed through November 25 at 20:00 UTC. Claude Code adds MCP-provided skills and a shell-command hook; Cognition introduces SWE-2.1 for coding. GitHub’s Fusion documentation now lists a December 31 discount cutoff. Earlier items retain their original dates, and the November 24 snapshot is preserved unchanged. The next-week forecast keeps its original criteria. No fresh timing rumor met the evidence threshold.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.332 adds MCP-provided skills in beta
items.summary: Skills served by MCP servers now appear in the slash menu under a server-qualified name. A new PreSkillShellCommand hook can reject inline shell commands when a skill or command loads. The release also improves recovery when an SSE MCP stream disconnects.
items.whyItMatters: Treat remote skill content as part of the trust boundary. Validate existing local policies against the new hook and check the runtime version across machines; older versions surface a startup dialog if the new hook is present.
items.historicalContext: Published November 25 at 01:32 UTC. This is a Claude Code release, not a universal MCP protocol rollout. MCP-provided skills specifically are beta.
items.confidenceReason: First-party documentation supports the reported update; independent behavior and workload costs were not tested.

sources.title: Claude Code v2.1.332
sources.authenticityReason: The publisher’s GitHub release records the date, beta status and hook behavior.

items.title: Added Nov 25: Cognition releases SWE-2.1 for coding workloads
items.summary: Cognition introduced SWE-2.1, a Kimi K3-based follow-up to SWE-2, and reports improved results on FrontierCode 2.0 and Terminal-Bench 4.1. The model is listed for Devin Desktop, Cloud, and CLI.
items.whyItMatters: Treat the scores as publisher-reported. Cognition’s comparisons combine results from different harnesses, so evaluate the model and harness together on your own coding tasks.
items.historicalContext: The announcement is dated November 24; added here without redating it. This entry concerns the standard software-engineering model.
items.confidenceReason: First-party documentation supports the reported update; independent behavior and workload costs were not tested.

sources.title: Introducing SWE-2.1

items.title: Billing watch: GitHub now lists the Fusion discount through Dec 31
items.summary: GitHub’s Fusion documentation says users on paid Copilot plans receive a 30% discount on model costs when using Fusion through December 31, 2026. The models used are billed at their applicable rates before the discount.
items.whyItMatters: Do not assume the older November 30 cutoff or apply this discount to non-Fusion model selection. For longer-running workloads, review actual usage and recheck the published terms before January.
items.historicalContext: The date is a documentation check, not the publication date of a new model or the exact day the terms changed. Copilot cloud sandbox compute is a separate cost.
items.confidenceReason: First-party documentation supports the reported update; independent behavior and workload costs were not tested.

items.title: Codex 0.172.0 restores sandbox context on exec resume
items.summary: The stable version restores the saved sandbox permissions, working directory and workspace roots on noninteractive resume unless explicitly overridden. The terminal UI can follow thread links; optional stdio MCP servers with cached tool lists start on first use.
items.whyItMatters: Check that reopened jobs retain their intended access boundary. Codex also adds an approval-reviewer setting for individual connected-app tools; test policy behavior before relying on it.
items.historicalContext: The publisher posted stable 0.172.0 on November 24 at 00:03 UTC. These are CLI changes, not a model or subscription-limit update.
items.confidenceReason: Confirmed in the publisher’s release documentation; behavior and performance have not been independently tested here.

items.title: Copilot CLI 1.0.115 adds ACP forms and sandbox fixes
items.summary: Supporting ACP editors can show structured clarification forms. Release notes include changes to Windows and macOS sandbox settings and a fix for sandboxed Git add and commit with many linked worktrees.
items.whyItMatters: Useful for editor integrations and agents sharing a repository through worktrees. Validate the target OS and client; ACP form support is conditional, and the CLI release alone does not establish SDK compatibility.
items.historicalContext: Published November 24 at 13:03 UTC. This CLI changelog is distinct from yesterday’s cloud sandbox billing milestone.
items.confidenceReason: Confirmed in the publisher’s release documentation; behavior and performance have not been independently tested here.

items.title: Added Nov 24: Claude Ship brings PR stewardship and approvals to beta
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Ship for Team and Enterprise plans with GitHub repositories. It pairs the existing generally available Code Review with PR Steward and Claude Approvals, both in beta.
items.whyItMatters: PR fixes and approval decisions are separate jobs. Review the repository approval policy and branch-protection interactions before enabling repository-wide automation; do not infer GitLab support.
items.historicalContext: The announcement is dated November 23, added in this review without redating. This is a code-delivery workflow, not a Claude model launch.
items.confidenceReason: Confirmed in the publisher’s release documentation; behavior and performance have not been independently tested here.

items.title: Added Nov 24: Strands ships Decider v2 weights and expands Box CLI support
items.summary: Strands published five Apache-2.0 Gemma 4-based decision models, from E2B to 31B. Its separate Box update adds native support for Claude Code, Codex, and Kiro CLI.
items.whyItMatters: Consider Decider for bounded option selection, not as a general coding-agent replacement. Calibrate fallback thresholds on your own task distribution. For Box, independently check what the sandbox permits rather than treating integration support as a security guarantee.
items.historicalContext: Both first-party announcements were dated November 23. Box is a sandbox integration, not a requirement to use Decider v2.
items.confidenceReason: Confirmed in the publisher’s release documentation; behavior and performance have not been independently tested here.

items.title: OpenAI adds Healthcare configurations to the Responses API
items.summary: OpenAI released Healthcare configurations for GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6.2 Sol, GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol. The configurations pair the models with a harness tailored to clinical questions; when web search is used, it draws from a dedicated medical-source index.
items.whyItMatters: This describes developer API behavior, not clinical validation, a substitute for licensed oversight, or a ChatGPT/Codex feature change.
items.historicalContext: A separate November 24 changelog entry refreshed the moving chat-latest API snapshot. It is not a fixed model ID or a new base-model launch.
items.confidenceReason: Confirmed in the publisher’s release documentation; behavior and performance have not been independently tested here.

items.title: GPT-6.2 Sol variant starts rolling out in ChatGPT Chat
items.summary: OpenAI began a global rollout of a conversation-tuned GPT-6.2 Sol variant in the Chat tab for Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise. Enterprise access depends on admin settings.
items.whyItMatters: OpenAI reports improvements on images and complex instructions in its Chat-tab evaluations. Those are publisher results, not independent coding benchmarks.
items.historicalContext: This is distinct from the November 17 GPT-6.2 launch. The November 23 Chat-tab release does not change Work or Codex models, or announce API pricing or subscription-limit changes.

items.title: OpenCode 2.4.0 adds scheduled and event-triggered automations
items.summary: The stable release supports one-off and recurring automations, cron schedules, and events from connected MCP servers. The automation manager exposes the resulting jobs, and the configuration can disable the feature.
items.whyItMatters: Audit what is allowed to run unattended. The release notes say a fixed shell action asks for approval at creation and logs the exit code and output for each run; do not assume it asks for fresh approval at every run.
items.historicalContext: This is a harness release, not a model launch. Its explicit background-task controls meet last edition’s November 23–29 forecast on November 23.
items.confidenceReason: Confirmed in first-party documentation; performance and behavior claims were not independently reproduced.

items.title: Anthropic starts Enterprise Frontier Safeguards beta
items.summary: The beta is available for eligible organizations on Claude Platform, Claude Platform on AWS, and Claude Models on Google Cloud when Anthropic-managed. Anthropic says it does not retain prompts or responses under EFS; encrypted safety copies go to a bucket in the customer’s cloud account.
items.whyItMatters: Zero data retention by Anthropic does not mean no copies exist. Workspaces using Anthropic-managed storage do not qualify as EFS. Verify eligibility and storage configuration before depending on it.
items.historicalContext: The November 23 platform update concerns safeguards for existing models, not a new model or general Mythos access.
items.confidenceReason: Confirmed in first-party documentation; performance and behavior claims were not independently reproduced.

items.whyItMatters: Inventory hard-coded model IDs and test the replacement before the cutoff. Check the schedule for the provider you actually use rather than assuming the Claude API date applies everywhere.
items.historicalContext: This is the November 23 deprecation announcement, not same-day API removal.
items.confidenceReason: Confirmed in first-party documentation; performance and behavior claims were not independently reproduced.

items.title: November 30–December 6: stable unattended-task control
items.summary: We expect at least one of Codex, Claude Code, Copilot CLI, or OpenCode to add or fix a user-visible control for unattended work.
items.whyItMatters: Scheduling is becoming useful only if developers can audit, pause, or stop jobs that run without them.
items.confidenceReason: Editorial extrapolation from OpenCode’s automation release and recent harness controls, not a publisher commitment or numeric probability.
items.historicalContext: OpenCode 2.4.0 provides a November 23 baseline and does not count toward this later forecast.

items.resolutionCriteria: Pass if official stable release notes for a named harness, published during the window, explicitly add or fix approval, disablement, cancellation, or per-run audit history for scheduled, event-triggered, or background jobs. Generic permissions, prereleases, documentation-only and model-only updates do not count. Otherwise fail at 23:59 UTC on December 6.
items.counterarguments: Maintainers may prioritize reliability or model support; automation changes may ship only as prereleases or outside the window.
